text: You're on the ground. The Murisk has a coil across your legs — not crushing, just weight, enough to keep you still. Its bioluminescent segments pulse close to your face. Then your own grunt comes back at you through its circular mouth: hollow, wet, delayed by half a beat.

options.text: > Try to pull your legs free

text: You stop moving. The echo stops too. The coil rests against you, heavy and warm. Its feeding seam parts slightly against your leg — not penetrating, just contact, tasting whatever it can read from your skin. Its blunt head lifts a few inches, then lowers again.
Your knee shifts. The Murisk's coil tightens — once, firm — then your own sharp exhale bounces back at you through its circular mouth, held half a beat longer than you made it. You go still.

The coil slowly draws back. Its bioluminescence dims from stressed-pale to a slow, rhythmic throb. The feeding seam closes. It doesn't retreat so much as it simply loses interest — coiling inward, the glow going dark by segment.
